html:
Travel agency · around Rome

Tours and day trips to the places travellers love.

Ancient sites, gardens, hill towns, lakes, beaches and snow. We take you where tourists really go around Rome, and a bit further when the season asks for it.

Explore destinationsAsk for a quote

Destinations

Close to Rome: the classics

The easiest and most popular day trips. Itineraries, dates and prices are being finalised.

Tivoli

Villa d’Este with its fountains and Hadrian’s Villa, an imperial estate.

Gardens · Archaeology

Ostia Antica

The well-preserved port city of ancient Rome, often compared with Pompeii.

Archaeology · Half day

Cerveteri

The Etruscan necropolis of Banditaccia, among the best-preserved in Italy.

Etruscans · Walking

Calcata

A tiny hilltop village of cafes, galleries and artists.

Village · Lunch

Castel Gandolfo & Nemi

Lakeside towns and the papal palace and gardens, with strawberries in season at Nemi.

Lakes · Views

Castelli Romani

Hill towns south-east of Rome known for food and local wine.

Wine · Food

Summer

Sea days

Anzio

About 40 km from Rome, with some of the area’s best beaches.

Beach · Seafood

Santa Marinella

Closest sea escape from the summer heat, season from late May to September.

Beach · Short ride

Sperlonga, Gaeta, Circeo

Whitewashed old towns and long beaches, longer day.

Beach · Old towns

Ponza

Island day by ferry, a Mediterranean escape that is quieter than most.

Island · Boat

Winter, December to March

Snow days, a bit further away

Skiing, snowboarding, sledding, tubing or a snowshoe walk. Rome’s own mountains are 1.5 to 2 hours away.

Monte Livata

About 75 km from Rome. Small resort with snowshoe trails, good for families.

Easiest · Snowshoes

Campo Staffi

About 100 km from Rome, with sledding and snow tubing besides the slopes.

Family · Sledding

Terminillo

“Rome’s mountain”, about 100 km away, with a snowpark and ski schools.

Ski · Snowpark

Campo Felice & Ovindoli

About 110 km from Rome, bigger slopes for medium and advanced skiers.

Ski · Snowboard

Campo Imperatore

On the Gran Sasso at 2,200 m, among the highest in Italy.

High altitude

Roccaraso

Central Italy’s largest ski area, a long day or a weekend.

Big ski area

Longer days

Further afield

Early start, late return. Worth it for a famous name.

Viterbo & Civita di Bagnoregio

Medieval towns, thermal springs and the “dying town” on its rock.

Orvieto & Assisi

Cathedral and underground city, then the basilica of St Francis.

Tuscany wine day

Siena, San Gimignano and a local vineyard by coach.

Florence

The Uffizi and the Duomo, by fast train or coach.

Naples & Pompeii

A very long day: pizza, the ruins and Vesuvius.

Amalfi Coast

Better as a weekend than a single day.

Where to stay

Need a base?

Our tours leave from the Mentana area, about 25 km from Rome. If you want to sleep nearby, a quiet villa with a garden is available for our travellers.

See the villa

Plan your trip

Tell us when you travel, how many you are and what you want to see.
